questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Task 5, control 1: a cardholder shall not spend more than $50,000 per year. How many cardholders spent more than $50,000 in 2014? Who spent the most, and how much?
questions.note: pcards_2013_2014.zip contains pcards.db with OSU transactions for calendar years 2013 and 2014. TransactionDate and PostedDate are stored as text like '7/26/2014 0:00:00'. Use the Year and Month columns for filtering.

mistakes.hint: That figure covers both years in the file. Restrict to 2014. The limit is per year.
You grouped on last name only. Different cardholders share a last name; use FullName (first initial + last name).

questions.prompt: Task 5, control 2: no more than $10,000 per month without approval. How many cardholder-month combinations exceeded $10,000 in 2014, and how many different cardholders are involved?

mistakes.hint: You grouped per cardholder for the whole year. Group by cardholder and month.

questions.prompt: Task 5, control 3: no single transaction may exceed $5,000. List all 2014 transactions for more than $5,000 (amount, cardholder, description, vendor, dates, MCC).
questions.note: pcards_2013_2014.zip contains pcards.db with OSU transactions for calendar years 2013 and 2014. TransactionDate and PostedDate are stored as text like '7/26/2014 0:00:00'. Use the Year and Month columns for filtering.

mistakes.hint: You included transactions of exactly $5,000. The limit is breached only by amounts more than $5,000 (> not >=).
That figure covers both years in the file. Restrict to 2014.
TransactionDate is text (e.g. '7/26/2014 0:00:00'), so comparing it with '2014' compares characters, not dates. Use the Year column, or LIKE '%/2014 %'.
Your total includes transactions of exactly $5,000. Use > 5000, not >= 5000.

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Task 5, control 4: an amount over $5,000 should not be split across several swipes by the same person. Find cardholder/vendor/day groups with more than one 2014 transaction and a combined total over $5,000. How many groups, and how many transactions do they contain in total?
questions.note: pcards_2013_2014.zip contains pcards.db with OSU transactions for calendar years 2013 and 2014. TransactionDate and PostedDate are stored as text like '7/26/2014 0:00:00'. Use the Year and Month columns for filtering. GROUP BY cardholder, vendor and TransactionDate with HAVING, then join back to list the transactions.

questions.subject: SQL
questions.prompt: Task 7, Q1: Benford's law. For 2014 transactions of $1.00 or more, what percentage of amounts begin with the digit 1, and with the digit 9? Give three decimals. (Benford expects about 30.1% and 4.6%.)
questions.note: pcards_2013_2014.zip contains pcards.db with OSU transactions for calendar years 2013 and 2014. TransactionDate and PostedDate are stored as text like '7/26/2014 0:00:00'. Use the Year and Month columns for filtering. The first character of CAST(Amount AS TEXT) gives the leading digit.

mistakes.hint: You included returns. Exclude amounts under 1.00, which removes the negative amounts too.
